scope: Proposition B.7 (A common finite success bound) of the manuscript “Memory and precision in noiseless Gaussian regression” (preprints/Memory-and-precision-in-noiseless-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a46ccc95821da009), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume d ≥ 16, set n = d − 1, p = ⌊d/8⌋, and let n/2 ≤ β ≤ d/2. Let M, T ≥ 0 be integers, 0 < ϵ ≤ 1/10, and consider a learner in Definition 1.1. Under the uniform-sphere signal prior, write Psucc for its success probability with either angular or chordal error at most ϵ, and put b = ⌈T/p⌉. Then Psucc ≤ min  1, 4n ϵn−β h Cd step (p + 2)2M 1/p ib  . (84) The same assertion holds with the initial factor 4n replaced by the polar-cap constant Cd 0 .
